text:
sam.sales: Heads-up — CoreBank ran a 45m POC and flagged severe p99 spikes during bursts. They asked for a short technical writeup explaining root causes, recommended config changes, and how that maps to pricing/commit options. Can we pull something together?
nina.sre: Yup. Can you paste the exact test details they ran? qps pattern, seq lengths, model, clients, any server flags?
sam.sales: From CoreBank:
  - model: open-redwood-3b-v2 (default FP16)
  - traffic: steady 40 qps, burst up to 160 qps for ~90s every 7m
  - clients: 32 worker threads from a single region
  - prompt tokens: mean 60, 95th=240, max 1024 (they included long docs)
  - batching: disabled server-side, client-side concatenation only
  - duration: 45m, warmup they did 2m
carlos.sales-eng: That config will cause very uneven batch formation. Long outlier sequences (1024) will force some kernels to run much longer and block GPU streams — that's a classic tail-driver. Also single-region client flood can hit network egress bursts and scheduler jitter.
mei.ml: Also check model memory working set: with variable seqs, KV cache churn increases memory pressure and can trigger memory compaction or small-page thrashing on some hosts. Short warmup means GPU clocks may not be stabilized.
nina.sre: Proposed quick fixes for the next run:
  1) enable server-side continuous batching with batch_timeout=5ms and max_batch=64
  2) instruct clients to attach session_id so we can enable prefix/KV cache for repeated flows
  3) cap input length at 512 for latency-sensitive endpoints or route long-docs to an async job
  4) extend warmup to 8-10m with the same burst pattern
  5) if strict high-percentile SLOs required, run on Dedicated (reserved) pool with pinned GPUs and no autoscaler during window
eli.se: For model variant: open-redwood-3b-v2 int8 gives ~2.2x throughput on our benchmark with a small eval delta (~0.7%). Combined with batching + cache that should flatten p95/p99 significantly.
tara.ciso: From a procurement/security angle they want: do we isolate logs, where are traces stored, and can we disable any server-side caches? Also curious about regional tenancy for EU data.
mei.ml: Answer: cache entries are opaque KV blobs tied to session ids; we can disable caching per-customer. Dedicated + VPC peering keeps logs in the customer's network egress and simplifies data residency. We store audit logs in their selected region for Dedicated/Private.
carlos.sales-eng: Test plan for re-run (45-60m measurement window):
  - ramp: 0 -> 40 qps over 4m, hold 20m, then intermittent bursts to 160 qps (90s) every 7m for 3 cycles
  - traffic: include 20% long-doc (512-1024) but route them to a different model tag in-case we need to compare
  - server: enable batching (5ms), max_batch=64, enable KV cache for sessioned traffic
  - metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999, mean batch size, GPU util, mem headroom, IPC, network latency by client region
eli.se: curl example for them to flip on batching and session id:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"open-redwood-3b-v2-int8","prompt":"<prompt>","max_tokens":256,"session_id":"corebank-2026-03"}'
nina.sre: Cost/commit notes for sales: rough delta estimates (high-level):
  - Hosted FP16: baseline per-token cost = 1.0x
  - Hosted int8: ~0.45x per-token
  - Dedicated int8 with 3xGPU committed pool: effective per-token ~0.28x after commit discounts (but depends on utilization)
  - Tradeoff: Dedicated increases fixed monthly cost but tightens percentile variability and gives stronger data residency controls.
eli.se: We should offer a managed run — our SEs will apply batching/cache and run the re-test, deliver Grafana snapshots + raw CSVs. Typical turnaround 24–48h.
tara.ciso: I'll draft a one-pager covering: data residency, encryption at rest & in transit, SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit log retention options, and instructions to opt out of cache. Drop it here by EOD.
sam.sales: Great. CoreBank also requested a plain-language blurb for their infra lead summarizing the fixes and impact on pricing — can someone create a 3-bullet summary I can paste in email?
mei.ml: Shareable 3-bullet summary:
  - Cause: p99 spikes driven by mixed long sequences + client-side batching causing small, irregular GPU batches and KV cache churn.
  - Short fixes: enable server-side batching (5ms), enable session-aware KV caching, and increase warmup to 8-10m — expect p95/p99 improvement ~30-60% depending on long-doc fraction.
  - If you need predictable sub-99.9 SLOs or strict EU data residency, choose Dedicated committed pool; it raises fixed costs but lowers per-token compute and reduces noisy-neighbor variability.
loadtest-bot: run finished: id=ct-20260312-04, failures=1 (timeout), avg=145ms, p95=380ms, p99=1120ms, p999=2200ms
sam.sales: Thanks — I'll propose the managed run + one-pager and offer the Dedicated pricing model for a 3-month pilot. I'll post the sample quote when carlos shares numbers.
carlos.sales-eng: Will calculate a 3-month committed quote vs 3-month hosted estimate and post by tomorrow AM.
eli.se: I'll prepare a Grafana dashboard export template (latency percentiles + batch heatmap + memory headroom) and attach to the managed POC package.
tara.ciso: One-pager uploaded to the company drive (link) — shared with thread.
sam.sales: Perfect — closing loop with CoreBank now. Thanks team :raised_hands:
